title: Run a customer pilot end to end
summary: Simulate a complete forward deployed engagement for a fictional customer, Northwind Benefits, whose case workers spend too long finding answers in a large set of policy documents. You will write the discovery summary and pilot plan, build a permission-aware question-answering service with citations over real public documents, create an evaluation set and measure against a baseline, package and deploy it with Docker Compose behind a login, prepare the security pack, run a demo, and hand it over with runbooks and an outcome report. Every artefact is something an FDE produces in a real engagement.
outcome: A public repository containing `docs/` (discovery summary, pilot plan, design note, security pack, outcome report, runbooks), `app/` (FastAPI service with permission-filtered retrieval and citations, Streamlit UI), `evals/` (question set, harness and results), and `deploy/` (Compose stack with health checks), plus a recorded 15-minute demo. Reviewers can follow your thinking from the customer's problem to a measured result.
prereqs: The stage 2 and 3 lessons of this track (discovery, scoping, customer data, communication, LLM apps, prototyping)
Access to any LLM API or a local model you can call from Python

tools.name: DuckDB

tools.name: pytest

phases.title: Set the scene and run discovery
phases.goal: A realistic customer context and a one-page discovery summary that defines the problem, users, data and success metric.

steps.text: Create the repository and folder layout.

code.code:
gh repo create northwind-pilot --public --clone && cd northwind-pilot
mkdir -p docs/runbooks data/raw app evals tests deploy

steps.text: Choose 40 to 80 public documents that stand in for Northwind's policies: for example a government's benefit guidance pages or public regulations saved as text or PDF. Put them in `data/raw/`.
steps.note: Use documents you are allowed to republish in a public repository; government publications are usually fine. Record the source of each in a `data/SOURCES.md`.

steps.text: Write the customer brief in your own words: Northwind's 60 case workers answer benefit questions by searching these documents; finding the right clause takes several minutes; mistakes cause appeals. Split the documents into two groups, `general` and `fraud-team`, and write `data/acl.csv` mapping each document to the groups allowed to read it.
Role-play two discovery interviews (ask a friend to be a case worker and a team lead) using the question bank from the discovery lesson, and record five facts with numbers and two quotes.
steps.note: If you have nobody to interview, write the answers you would expect and mark them clearly as assumptions to validate.

steps.text: Write `docs/01-discovery-summary.md` with the eight sections from the discovery lesson, ending with the decision you request: proceed to a six-week pilot for the general case-worker team.
steps.check: Someone who has never heard of the project can explain the problem, the user and the metric after reading it.

phases.title: Scope the pilot
phases.goal: A pilot plan with success criteria, boundaries, dependencies, risks and a decision date.

steps.text: Write `docs/02-pilot-plan.yaml` with users, duration, primary metric (median time to answer a case question), guardrails (answer accuracy, citation correctness, no restricted-document leaks) and in-scope and out-of-scope lists.

code.code:
pilot: northwind-policy-assistant
duration_weeks: 6
users: 10 general case workers
success_criteria:
  primary: median time to answer a case question down >= 40% vs baseline
  guardrails:
    - correct answer on >= 90% of 60 expert-checked questions
    - every answer cites at least one source
    - zero answers drawn from documents the user may not read
in_scope: [general policy documents, web UI behind login, English]
out_of_scope: [writing to case systems, mobile, other languages]
decision: sponsor go/no-go at end of week 6

steps.text: Add a dependencies table (document export, SSO registration, security review slot, expert reviewer time) with owners and dates, and a risk register with at least five risks.
steps.note: Put both in the YAML or a markdown file next to it; what matters is owners and dates.

steps.text: Write `docs/03-design-note.md` comparing two hosting options for the model (a hosted API with zero-retention terms versus a self-hosted open model) and recommend one with reasons.
steps.check: The note ends with 'Decision needed from: ... by: ...'.

phases.title: Ingest documents with permissions
phases.goal: Every chunk indexed with its source, heading and access groups, ready for keyword search.

steps.text: Create the environment.

code.code:
uv init --app . && uv add fastapi uvicorn streamlit duckdb pypdf httpx pydantic
uv add --dev pytest ruff

steps.text: Write the ingestion script: extract text, split by headings into chunks of at most 1,500 characters, attach `doc_id`, `heading` and `groups`, and load everything into DuckDB with a full-text index.
steps.check: The script prints a chunk count, and documents missing from acl.csv are reported rather than silently readable by everyone (add that check).

steps.text: Make documents without an ACL entry fail loudly instead of defaulting to readable: in `ingest.py`, collect any doc_id not in `acl` and exit with an error listing them.
steps.note: Defaulting to open is the classic permission leak.

phases.title: Retrieve with permissions and answer with citations
phases.goal: An API that only ever uses passages the user may read and cites them in every answer.

steps.text: Write retrieval: full-text search, then filter by the user's groups before anything else happens.

code.code:
# app/retrieve.py
import duckdb

con = duckdb.connect("data/index.duckdb", read_only=True)
con.execute("LOAD fts")


def search(question: str, user_groups: set[str], k: int = 6) -> list[dict]:
    rows = con.execute(
        """SELECT id, doc_id, heading, groups, body,
                  fts_main_chunks.match_bm25(id, ?) AS score
           FROM chunks WHERE score IS NOT NULL ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 50""",
        [question]).fetchall()
    allowed = [r for r in rows if user_groups & set(r[3].split("|"))]
    return [{"id": r[0], "doc_id": r[1], "heading": r[2], "text": r[4]} for r in allowed[:k]]

steps.text: Write a test proving a general user never receives a fraud-team document, even for a question that matches it exactly.

code.code:
# tests/test_permissions.py
from app.retrieve import search


def test_general_user_cannot_see_fraud_docs():
    hits = search("fraud investigation procedures", {"general"})
    assert all(h["doc_id"] != "fraud-investigation-procedures" for h in hits)


def test_fraud_team_can_see_them():
    hits = search("fraud investigation procedures", {"fraud-team"})
    assert any(h["doc_id"] == "fraud-investigation-procedures" for h in hits)

steps.text: Write the API with health, readiness and an `/ask` endpoint that builds a cited prompt from allowed passages and calls your model through one `call_llm` function.
steps.note: Unknown users get no groups and therefore no documents: deny by default.

steps.text: Add a `/readyz` endpoint that returns 503 if the index cannot be opened or the model call fails a tiny test prompt.
steps.check: Stopping the model or deleting the index makes /readyz return 503.

phases.title: Evaluate against a baseline
phases.goal: Numbers for accuracy, citations and leak-safety, plus a measured time-to-answer comparison.

steps.text: Write 60 evaluation questions in `evals/questions.csv` with the expected answer, the source document and the asking group; include ten questions whose answer is not in the documents and five that would require fraud-team documents asked as a general user.

code.code:
question,expected,source_doc,group
What is the maximum housing support period?,12 months,housing-support-2025,general
What is the penalty for late renewal?,NOT_IN_DOCS,,general

steps.text: Write `evals/run_evals.py` to call `/ask` for each question and record: whether the expected source was cited, whether the answer contains the expected fact (manual review or a calibrated judge), whether 'not found' was said when expected, and whether any restricted document appeared.
steps.note: For the correctness column, a simple first pass is to review 60 answers by hand; it takes under an hour and is exactly what customer experts would do.

steps.text: Measure the baseline: time yourself (or a volunteer) answering ten questions by searching the raw documents manually, then answering ten different questions with the assistant. Record times per question.
steps.check: You have two lists of times and can compute medians.

steps.text: Change one thing (chunk size, k, or the prompt), rerun the evaluation, and keep whichever version scores better; record both results.
steps.note: One variable at a time, as in the inference track.

phases.title: Package, secure and deploy
phases.goal: A Compose stack a customer could run, with health checks, configuration from the environment and a security pack.

steps.text: Write a Dockerfile for the API (non-root user, pinned base) and one for the UI, then a Compose file with health checks and configuration from an env file.

code.code:
# deploy/compose.yml
services:
  api:
    build: {context: .., dockerfile: deploy/Dockerfile.api}
    env_file: ../.env
    volumes: ["../data:/app/data:ro"]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8000/healthz')"]
      interval: 15s
  ui:
    build: {context: .., dockerfile: deploy/Dockerfile.ui}
    environment: {API_URL: "http://api:8000"}
    ports: ["8501:8501"]
    depends_on: {api: {condition: service_healthy}}

steps.text: Build and start the stack and confirm the UI answers questions with sources.

code.code:
cp .env.example .env   # model endpoint and key, never committed
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml up -d --build
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml ps

steps.check: Both services show healthy; http://localhost:8501 works.

steps.text: Write `docs/04-security-pack.md`: a data-flow table for every arrow, a STRIDE list with at least eight threats and mitigations, and answers to the seven standard and seven AI-specific questions from the security-review lesson.
steps.note: Be honest about what a pilot lacks (for example real SSO) and how production would close it.

phases.title: Demo, measure, hand over
phases.goal: A recorded demo, an outcome report with a decision request, and documentation that lets someone else run it.

steps.text: Prepare a seeded demo of eight questions (six that show value, one 'not found', one permission refusal) and record a 15-minute demo following the problem, live case, evidence, limits and ask structure.
steps.check: The recording shows the permission refusal working live.

steps.text: Write `docs/05-outcome-report.md`: decision requested, headline result with medians, evaluation table, ROI estimate with written assumptions and a range, what did not work, and the proposed next phase.
steps.note: Use the ROI template from the outcomes lesson; label any assumed numbers clearly.

steps.text: Write three runbooks in `docs/runbooks/` (re-index after new documents, rotate the model API key, everything answers 'not found') in the symptoms, check, fix, verify, escalate format.
Ask a friend to follow your README and runbooks to run the stack and re-index from scratch without your help; fix every step where they stalled.
steps.check: They succeed without asking you a question.

steps.text: Tidy, commit and publish; delete any API keys from your environment files and rotate the key you used for testing.

code.code:
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml down
git add -A && git commit -m "Northwind pilot: discovery to outcome report" && git push

troubleshooting.symptom: DuckDB says the fts extension is not installed
troubleshooting.fix: Run `INSTALL fts; LOAD fts` once with network access (the ingest script does this); in an offline environment, pre-download the extension. Retrieval loads it read-only after ingestion.

troubleshooting.symptom: Answers ignore the sources or invent facts
troubleshooting.fix: Check whether retrieval returned the right passage (print hits). If it did, tighten the instruction and lower temperature; if not, fix chunking or add keyword variants. Add the case to the evaluation set.

troubleshooting.symptom: A general user sees a fraud-team document
troubleshooting.fix: Treat it as a sev-1 bug: check acl.csv for the document, confirm ingestion failed loudly on missing ACLs, and make sure filtering happens in search() before the prompt is built. Add the case to tests.

troubleshooting.symptom: PDF text comes out empty or garbled
troubleshooting.fix: The PDF may be scanned images; use a text version of the document or add OCR, and note it as a data-quality finding in the discovery summary.

troubleshooting.symptom: The UI cannot reach the API inside Compose
troubleshooting.fix: Use the service name (http://api:8000), not localhost, from the UI container, and check the API health check passes.

next: Replace the hard-coded user groups with a real OIDC login (for example a local Keycloak) and read groups from the token.
Add vector search and combine it with BM25 (hybrid), then measure recall@k before and after.
Deploy the stack to a local Kubernetes cluster with the Helm practices from the packaging lesson.
Run a second simulated customer with different documents and refactor customer-specific parts into configuration.
Turn the outcome report into a short case study and add it to your portfolio.
